info.title: Steward API
info.description:
Read-only access to the data Steward holds: processes and their versions, runs with their step journal and logs, decisions, schedules, webhook triggers, platform metadata, dashboard datasets, the audit log, users and teams, monitors (status, history, Zabbix low-level discovery), the credentials register (documentation only, never secret values), and the data model itself as an Apache Ossie semantic model.

**Authentication.** Every endpoint except `/health` needs a personal API token: `Authorization: Bearer smt_…`. Create one on your profile page in the web UI (scope *read* is enough; tokens with scope *mcp* only work on the MCP endpoint). A token acts with the rights of its owner – use a dedicated service account with the *viewer* or *auditor* role for integrations. Session cookies are not accepted.

**Conventions.** JSON with camelCase fields; timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC; ids are strings. Lists return `{ items, nextCursor }` – pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get the next page (also offered as an RFC 8288 `Link: <…>; rel="next"` header). `limit` is 1–200 (default 50). Errors are problem details (RFC 9457, `application/problem+json`). Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store` and `RateLimit-*` headers; above the limit the API answers 429 with `Retry-After`.

**Versioning.** The path carries the major version. Within v1 changes are additive (new endpoints, optional parameters and fields) – ignore fields you do not know. Breaking changes get a new major version; endpoints that are going away are announced with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers first.

get.description: Datasets (the API resources), fields with types, relationships and metrics such as the run success rate or monitor availability, as an [Apache Ossie](https://github.com/apache/ossie) (formerly OSI) document. JSON or YAML (`Accept: application/yaml` or `format=yaml`). The model describes the schema, not data, and is the same for every token. See docs/SEMANTIC-MODEL.md.

get.description: Returns `{"data":[{"{#MONITOR}":"machine-17-powermeter","{#CHECK}":"pm-reachable",…}]}` for a Zabbix HTTP agent discovery rule. Use the macros in item prototypes, e.g. a dependent item on `/monitors/{#MONITOR}/status` with JSONPath `$.checks[?(@.checkId=="{#CHECK}")].statusCode.first()`.
